findings.summary: all three cited test names are SPLIT across two {@code} spans, so none of them greps -- the checkability the enumeration rests on
findings.detail: `{@code ...aReplayFromBELOWThePointerIsREFUSED_NotApplied}` + `{@code Twice}` (:86-87), `{@code ...aReplayThePointedDeltaDoesNotCarry}` + `{@code IsREFUSED}` (:87-88), and `{@code DedupAcrossTakeoverTest.aBAREV0Checkpoint}` + `{@code SlotLeavesItsPodUNPROTECTED_AndThatIsRecorded}` (:109-110). Each renders with a space in the middle of an identifier, and `grep -rn aReplayFromBELOWThePointerIsREFUSED_NotAppliedTwice sequencer/src/main` returns nothing today (measured). The commit's whole argument for naming rather than counting is that a name can be checked; a name split by the 100-column wrap cannot be checked by grep or by a future rung-3 gate of the obvious shape ('every Class.method cited in src/main javadoc resolves to a @Test method'), which is what non-negotiable 9 would ask for here.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.52 writes the incarnation pin and renames or moves `aReplayFromBELOWThePointerIsREFUSED_NotAppliedTwice` while reorganising `DedupAcrossTakeoverTest`. A grep for the old name across the tree finds no citation, so this enumeration keeps naming a test that no longer exists -- the same silent staleness as the wrong counts this row exists to retire, one level down.

findings.summary: the class javadoc now defers to Sequencer's list, but `seed`'s own javadoc in the same file still restates the superseded-incarnation limit in full
findings.detail: The staged change rewrites the class javadoc to 'STATED BY REFERENCE AND NOT RESTATED HERE ... two `src/main` statements of the same property disagreeing is what M5.34 exists to end'. Twelve lines further down, `seed`'s javadoc still says in full: 'Checkpoint.pods is keyed by podId, so it remembers a pod's LATEST incarnation only. A replay from an incarnation that has since been superseded is therefore not answered, and lands twice ... the direction that duplicates'. It is ACCURATE today, so this is not a correctness finding and not blocking -- but it is a second src/main statement of an enumerated limit, which is the condition the sentence twelve lines above declares ended. (`ChainReplay.java:322-344` holds a third, for the bare v0 slot; that one reads as local mechanism at the skip itself and is harder to argue away.)
findings.failure_scenario: M5.52 closes or narrows the superseded-incarnation limit, updates `Sequencer`'s list because that is the file M5.34 named as the single enumeration, and leaves `IdempotencyWindow.seed` asserting 'lands twice' about behaviour that no longer does. A caller reading the seam it actually calls gets the retired sentence.
